name: ESR1 mutation
summary: ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations are rarely present in primary breast cancer but are acquired under aromatase inhibitor selection in metastatic disease, causing ligand-independent ER activity and predicting benefit from oral SERDs.
biology: Missense mutations in the ESR1 ligand-binding domain stabilise helix 12 in the agonist conformation, enabling constitutive, oestrogen-independent ER transcriptional activity. Because aromatase inhibitors act by depriving the receptor of ligand, these mutations confer resistance to oestrogen deprivation, and some (notably Y537S) also reduce sensitivity to tamoxifen and fulvestrant.

methods: Plasma ctDNA NGS or digital PCR (preferred owing to polyclonal and evolving nature)
Tissue NGS of a recent metastatic biopsy
testing.notes: Testing should be repeated at progression, as ESR1 mutations emerge during therapy; testing archival primary tumour is not informative.

predictiveRelevance: ESR1 mutation predicts benefit from elacestrant over standard endocrine therapy after prior endocrine therapy including a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Additional oral SERDs and switching strategies guided by serial ctDNA monitoring have been evaluated in trials.
resistance: Polyclonal ESR1 mutations with variable SERD sensitivity
Concurrent PI3K pathway alterations and cell-cycle alterations
